trigger.summary: Initial reading proved that downstream state can redefine template ownership and applied-version evidence.
trigger.root_cause: One reconciliation block owns release policy, local observation, baseline hashes, and version convergence, then rebuilds them by scanning downstream.

posture_evidence.summary: Published template tags have active downstream manifests, including PersonalAssistant 4.7.0.
posture_evidence.ref: GitHub release v4.9.0 and PersonalAssistant preflight 2026-07-19

product.user_victory: A downstream operator can preview and apply one pinned template tag without losing local work or receiving a false convergence signal.
product.final_path: Exact release payload through deterministic ownership policy, conflict-safe apply, isolated packaging, and verified publication.
product.falsifier: A local source-absent file enters the manifest, a repeated conflict overwrites local content, a secret appears in dry-run or argv, or publish shares write authority with installers.

change.summary: Replace self-mutating downstream reconciliation with release-payload ownership and staged legacy AGENTS migration.
change.scope: Template sync reconciliation, MCP merge output, release workflow isolation, focused tests, and release-facing version docs.

options.summary: Add exclusions for currently known local files while retaining downstream scanning and global rehashing.

evidence.summary: A narrow exclusion would stop the current .codex README example.

data_safety.reason: Unknown local paths and repeated conflict rehashing remain capable of future overwrite.

security.reason: The self-ownership path remains available for other managed-looking downstream paths.

protected_contracts.reason: Project-owned downstream files are not protected generically by path exclusions.

evidence.summary: Focused exclusions can be fixture-tested but do not prove the general invariant.
The narrow source patch remains revertable in git.

product_outcome.basis: Unknown local files remain exposed under the same algorithm.
product_outcome.baseline: Current downstream scan accepts arbitrary immediate files.

business_outcome.basis: The patch does not change release lead time reliably.

correctness.baseline: Conflict hash is replaced by local hash.

maintainability.basis: Every new collision requires another exclusion.
maintainability.baseline: One generic downstream scan owns all paths.

reliability.basis: Convergence still depends on untrusted local directory contents.

performance.basis: No comparable performance change is expected.

security.basis: Unknown ownership poisoning and secret output remain possible.
security.baseline: Generic path and full JSON output exist.

transition_cost.basis: A narrow exclusion is smaller to implement initially.
transition_cost.baseline: Systemic repair changes reconciliation and tests.
transition_cost.result: One exclusion needs fewer changed modules.

total_cost.basis: Low initial diff but recurring exclusions and incident risk remain.

options.summary: Use target release payload as the only source of template ownership and migrate legacy AGENTS only when conflict-safe.

evidence.summary: Existing sync phases already expose target payload, old hashes, and conflict output needed by the replacement.
The design never adopts source-absent local files and preserves conflicting local content.
Least-privilege job permissions and redacted secret handling remove the identified trust paths.
evidence.ref: GitHub Actions GITHUB_TOKEN official guidance and local MCP sentinel test

evidence.summary: Manifest JSON shape, CLI flags, project files, and conflict artifacts remain preserved.
Safe, conflicting, poisoned, repeated, redaction, and workflow fixtures cover each exploit path.
The source patch is revertable and legacy apply remains preview-first with local conflicts untouched.

product_outcome.basis: The operator gets truthful convergence and preserved local work.
product_outcome.baseline: v4.9.0 can advance version and poison ownership.
product_outcome.result: Target-only ownership and conflict-gated versioning remove both paths.
product_outcome.ref: PersonalAssistant preflight and legacy fixture contract

business_outcome.basis: Preventing false rollout and recovery work reduces downstream support load.
business_outcome.result: One fixture-backed patch release supports a deterministic preview gate.

correctness.basis: Ownership, baseline hash, and applied version become separate decisions.
correctness.baseline: One block scans, rehashes, and advances all state.
correctness.result: Only applied target files update hashes and zero conflicts advance version.

maintainability.basis: One source payload rule replaces path-by-path downstream exclusions.
maintainability.baseline: Local directory contents implicitly extend ownership.
maintainability.result: Only target payload additions can enter ownership.

reliability.basis: Repeated sync keeps conflicts stable instead of turning them into overwrites.
reliability.baseline: Conflict rehash changes the next run decision.
reliability.result: Conflict baseline and version remain unchanged.

performance.basis: No performance advantage is claimed without a comparable benchmark.

security.basis: Secrets leave argv/output and write permission is limited to the publish job.
security.baseline: Full MCP JSON and job-wide write permission exist.
security.result: Sentinel redaction and job isolation are explicit invariants.
security.ref: GitHub Actions token guidance and security review

transition_cost.basis: The systemic replacement requires more fixtures and workflow changes than exclusions.

reversibility.basis: Conflict state remains recoverable and release artifact identity is checked between isolated jobs.
reversibility.baseline: Manifest evidence mutates before conflict resolution.
reversibility.result: Source commit and downstream preview provide explicit rollback points.
reversibility.ref: staged release and sync rollback plan

total_cost.basis: Higher one-time verification cost removes recurring ownership and release incident paths.

cleanup.removal_condition: Remove downstream directory scanning and job-wide write permission in the same patch before tagging.
cleanup.absence_check: Search for addManagedTree downstream reconciliation, full MCP JSON dry-run output, and workflow-level contents write; run regression and release gates.

recommendation.reason: Bounded replacement removes the proven duplicate ownership and version-state path while preserving the public manifest and CLI contracts.
recommendation.rejected_alternative: Known-file exclusions leave generic ownership poisoning, conflict rehashing, and repeated silent overwrite intact.

envelope.outcome: Publish a production-safe v4.9.1 that can preview legacy downstream projects without losing local work or secrets.
envelope.scope: Template source sync, MCP merge, release workflow, regression fixtures, version declarations, and release docs only.
envelope.risk_limit: HIGH template and release risk with no destructive downstream apply before a clean pinned preview.
envelope.downtime_limit: No downstream runtime downtime and no automatic modification of PersonalAssistant during source repair.
envelope.cost_limit: Remain inside the requested production repair and patch-release work.
envelope.release_limit: Publish only v4.9.1 after local and GitHub validation gates pass; never move or replace v4.9.0 assets.
envelope.environment_limit: Source repository, synthetic fixtures, isolated GitHub runners, and read-only PersonalAssistant preview after publication.
envelope.rollback_requirement: Keep one revertable source commit, immutable old tag, checksum-bound artifact, and conflict-preserving downstream behavior.
invalidation_conditions: release workflow cannot bind exact tag and artifact
